curation.lead:
The Epstein Network is the integrated assemblage of corporate entities, trusts, foundations, banks, and professional fiduciaries through which Jeffrey Epstein moved capital, managed property, and brokered relationships from the early 1990s until his death in August 2019 [Finding #622]. Probate filings in U.S. Virgin Islands Superior Court inventoried the estate at $577,672,654 [EFTA00027979], consisting of approximately $180.6 million in real property held through six single-asset USVI corporations — Maple Inc (9 East 71st Street, New York; $55.9 million), Nautilus Inc (Little St. James; $63.9 million), Great St. James ($22.5 million), Cypress Inc (Zorro Ranch, New Mexico; $17.2 million), Laurel Inc (El Brillo Way, Palm Beach; $12.4 million), and SCI JEP (Paris; $8.7 million) [Finding #622] — plus $194,986,301 in hedge fund and private-equity positions [Finding #622]. A 2006 JPMorgan data-tape inventory referenced 23 affiliated accounts [Finding #623] spanning J. Epstein and Company, Financial Trustees Inc, Forums LLC, Palm Beach Trust, the Zorro Trust, the J. Epstein Foundation, the COUQ Foundation, New York Strategy Group LLC, NES LLC, JEGE Inc, and corporate vehicles for Ghislaine Maxwell [Finding #623] [EFTA01340334].

Trust and probate documents show fiduciary control was concentrated in a small group [Finding #609]. The 2007 Jeffrey E. Epstein Insurance Trust #3 named attorney Darren Indyke as trustee, with accountant Richard Kahn added effective December 17–27, 2012 [Finding #609] [EFTA00016865]; Deutsche Bank analyst Mayur Rathod ran KYC and adverse-media screening on the trust and cleared it, recording that prior sex-offense charges had been resolved [Finding #609]. The 2001 Trust One was modified to remove Jeffrey A. Schantz as co-trustee and to designate Ghislaine Maxwell and Ira Zicherman as successor co-trustees [EFTA01266298], and Epstein's will routed all property to that trust with executors Indyke, Joseph Pagano, and Lawrence Newman, and backup executors Jes Staley and Andrew Farkas [Finding #609]. A parallel nonprofit tier — Gratitude America Ltd, International Peace Institute, the Humpty Dumpty Institute, the Kuhn Foundation, the Enhanced Education and COUQ Foundation USVI shells, and the Wexner, Leon Black, and Dubin family foundations — reached approximately $40 million in identifiable combined assets [Finding #462], declining roughly 60% by 2022 [Finding #462].

Following Epstein's July 2019 arrest and August 2019 death, entities under direct Epstein control entered dormancy or sustained decline while donor-driven entities continued to operate [Finding #447]. Gratitude America — capitalized by a $10 million 2015 transfer from Leon Black — froze at $8.175 million with zero activity after 2020 [Finding #1535], the Edge Foundation collapsed from roughly $501,000 to $74,000 [Finding #1535], and the Dubin Family Foundation wound down from $806,000 to $4,000 [Finding #1535]. Ten Epstein-created entities were named in the November 2022 USVI Attorney General settlement [Finding #447], and the disposition of frozen Gratitude America assets and of the three USVI foundations absent from federal IRS 990 filings — the J Epstein VI Foundation, Enhanced Education, and the COUQ Foundation — remains unresolved [Finding #447].
curation.system_role: The Epstein Network is a documented case in which a single principal assembled a multi-jurisdictional structure — USVI shell corporations, layered trusts, IRS-exempt and unfiled foundations, concentrated fiduciary roles, and bank relationships at firms including JPMorgan and Deutsche Bank — that aligned property holding, advisory income, charitable disbursement, and political access into a single managed system, while remaining largely outside the disclosure regimes (Lobbying Disclosure Act registration, federal 990 filings, public corporate registries) that ordinarily make such activity legible to regulators and the public.

sections.content:
Probate filings in U.S. Virgin Islands Superior Court [EFTA00027979] listed total estate property of $577,672,654 organized around six single-asset USVI corporations [Finding #622]. Maple Inc held the New York townhouse at 9 East 71st Street, valued at $55,931,000 [Finding #622]; Nautilus Inc held Little St. James at $63,874,223 [Finding #622]; Great St. James was valued at $22,498,600 [Finding #622]; Cypress Inc held the Zorro Ranch in New Mexico at $17,246,208 [Finding #622]; Laurel Inc held the El Brillo Way property in Palm Beach at $12,380,209 [Finding #622]; and SCI JEP held the Paris apartment at $8,672,823 [Finding #622]. Each property entity was capitalized with 10,000 shares except SCI JEP (999 shares), and hedge fund and private-equity positions added $194,986,301 to the inventoried value [Finding #622] [EFTA00027979].

A separate operational and financial layer ran in parallel to the property holders [Finding #623]. A 2006 JPMorgan data-tape inventory transmitted in a September 2009 letter from JPM Vice President Janet Young to Richard Kahn and Darren Indyke referenced 23 affiliated accounts containing Social Security numbers, tax identifiers, names, and addresses [Finding #623] [EFTA01340334]: 116 East 65th St LLC, Arts Interests, ASW Holdings LLC, Commun Interests, EGC Capital LLC, Jeffrey E. Epstein, Financial Trustees Inc, Forums LLC, Health and Science Interests, Heritage Interests, Institutional Interests, International Charitable Interest II, J. Epstein and Company, J. Epstein Foundation, JEGE Inc, Ghislaine Maxwell, NES LLC, New York Strategy Group LLC, Palm Beach Trust, Ranch Lake II Inc, Ranch Lake III Inc, the COUQ Foundation, and the Zorro Trust [Finding #623]. JPMorgan represented in writing that it had no evidence the data had been used inappropriately and offered Chase Identity Protection to affected parties [Finding #623] [EFTA01340334].

The USVI structure is not incidental to the network's composition [Finding #447]. Three Epstein-controlled foundations — the J Epstein VI Foundation, Enhanced Education, and the COUQ Foundation — do not appear in federal IRS 990 filings, while comparable U.S.-incorporated entities such as Gratitude America Ltd and the International Peace Institute filed annually [Finding #447]. Cross-reference of 990 records and probate filings indicates the USVI tier sits outside the federal nonprofit transparency regime that captures the rest of the network [Finding #447] [Finding #462].

sections.title: Fiduciary Control Structure
sections.content:
Trust and will documents concentrate decision rights in a small set of professional fiduciaries [Finding #609]. The 2007 Jeffrey E. Epstein Insurance Trust #3, dated November 1, 2007, named Darren Indyke as trustee, with Richard Kahn added as additional trustee effective December 17–27, 2012 [Finding #609] [EFTA00016865]. Deutsche Bank ran a KYC and adverse-media review on Insurance Trust #3 (analyst Mayur Rathod) and cleared it for onboarding, noting in its file that Epstein's prior sex-offense charges had been resolved [Finding #609]. The DugganUSA corpus contains 258 documents that reference the trust [Finding #609].

Earlier, the 2001 Trust One was reorganized to remove Jeffrey A. Schantz as co-trustee and to designate Ghislaine Maxwell and Ira Zicherman as successor co-trustees [EFTA01266298] [Finding #609], with the trust instrument stating: "I hereby remove JEFFREY A. SCHANTZ as a co-Trustee of the trust and designate GHISLAINE MAXWELL and IRA ZICHERMAN as successor co-Trustees in his place" [EFTA01266298]. Epstein's will then directed all property to the 2001 Trust, naming Indyke, Joseph Pagano, and Lawrence Newman as executors and Jes Staley and Andrew Farkas as backup executors [Finding #609] [EFTA01298228].

The same fiduciary group recurs across the operational entities [Finding #1535]. Officer-level review of 990 filings places Kahn, Indyke, and Erika Kellerhals at Gratitude America, while Leon Black's family-foundation board included Apollo executives Hannan and Cohen, and the Humpty Dumpty Institute carried Mark Epstein on its board [Finding #1535]. FEC employer fields confirm only four Epstein-controlled entities ever functioned as employers in any federal donation record — J Epstein and Company / Epstein and Company Inc, New York Strategy Group LLC, Ossa Properties Inc, and RDK Properties LLC [Finding #478] — with the core advisory and nonprofit shells (Gratitude America, Enhanced Education, DKIP, Financial Trust Company) producing zero employer-tagged donations [Finding #469].

sections.title: Nonprofit Grant Flow
sections.content:
Cross-reference of IRS 990 filings across approximately twelve network nonprofits identifies a multi-tier grant-flow pattern between 2012 and 2023 [Finding #1535]. Gratitude America received a $10 million capitalization from Leon Black in October 2015 [Finding #1535] and subsequently disbursed grants to the International Peace Institute ($375,000), the Edge Foundation ($35,000), the Ricardo O'Gorman Garden ($30,000), MIT ($150,000), the Kuhn Foundation ($650,000), and Humanity Plus ($100,000) [Finding #1535], with reported grant totals of $1.26 million in 2017 and $891,000 in 2018 [Finding #1535]. The Black Family Foundation separately funded the Clinton Foundation ($750,000), the Tony Blair Foundation ($250,000), and Birthright Israel ($1.5 million) [Finding #1535].

Comparative review of 990 filings groups network nonprofits into four trajectories [Finding #447]: frozen post-arrest — Gratitude America at $8.175 million with zero activity since 2020 [Finding #447]; sustained decline — IPI from $11.6 million to $5.9 million in assets over thirteen years, the Humpty Dumpty Institute losing roughly 80% of revenue from a $1.8 million peak, and the Edge Foundation declining from $501,000 to $74,000 [Finding #447] [Finding #1535]; absent from federal records — the J Epstein VI Foundation, Enhanced Education, and the COUQ Foundation [Finding #447]; and unaffected — the Wexner Foundation continuing at $10–15 million per year and the Ricardo O'Gorman Garden growing [Finding #447]. Total identifiable network nonprofit assets were approximately $40.4 million across ten entities [Finding #462], with a peak of approximately $50–60 million circa 2010–2014 and an estimated 60% subsequent contraction [Finding #462].

Recurring officer overlap accompanied the grant flow [Finding #1535]. Officer-level review of 990s places Kahn, Indyke, and Kellerhals at Gratitude America; Brockman and Matson at the Edge Foundation; Cwerman with Mark Epstein at the Humpty Dumpty Institute; and Apollo executives Hannan and Cohen at the Black Family Foundation [Finding #1535]. The IRS flagged the HDI for an excess-benefit transaction in 2015 [Finding #1535], and the Edge Foundation received a $35,000 grant from Gratitude America in 2018 while itself making zero grants in the same filing year [Finding #1535].

sections.title: Political Access and Disclosure Posture
sections.content:
The network's political activity is concentrated in FEC individual contributions rather than in registered lobbying [Finding #441] [Finding #480]. Cross-reference of FEC records across more than twenty network individuals identifies four Epstein entities ever appearing in employer fields [Finding #478]: J. Epstein and Company / Epstein and Company Inc (used by Jeffrey Epstein's personal donations 1994–2000 and by Indyke in 2000) [Finding #478], New York Strategy Group LLC (used by Indyke in 2003, Lesley Groff 2007–2014, and Jeffrey A. Schantz in 2002) [Finding #478], Ossa Properties Inc (used by Anthony Barrett 2000–2020 and Mark Epstein 1999–2021) [Finding #478], and RDK Properties LLC (used by Richard Kahn in 2007) [Finding #478]. Donations from employees of Gratitude America, Enhanced Education, DKIP, and Financial Trust Company do not appear in any FEC filing [Finding #469].

FEC bundling analysis identifies three coordinated clusters that map to officials with jurisdictional oversight of Epstein property [Finding #476]. The USVI cluster directed funds to Delegate Stacey Plaskett from Indyke ($8,000 across 2014–2018) and Groff ($2,600 in 2014) [Finding #476]. The New Mexico cluster, where Cypress Inc held Zorro Ranch, directed maximum contributions of $2,300 each from Indyke, Kahn, and Ken Starr to Bill Richardson within months of one another, plus $4,000 each from Ghislaine Maxwell and Indyke to King for Congress (NM) [Finding #476]. The Clinton cluster combined contributions from Maxwell, Kahn, Barrett, and Alan Dershowitz totalling roughly $5,800 in 2007, alongside Epstein's $20,000 contribution to the 1999 Hillary Clinton Senate campaign [Finding #476].

Direct giving by Epstein himself ceased after 2000 [Finding #471], while his fiduciary circle continued giving through 2018 with Epstein entities listed as employer [Finding #471] [Finding #480]. Cross-reference of FEC and Lobbying Disclosure Act records shows zero LDA filings for Epstein personally, the IPI, the Humpty Dumpty Institute, Gratitude America, Enhanced Education, the Leon Black Foundation, or any Epstein-named entity [Finding #441], while Apollo Global Management reported $1.21 million in 2019 lobbying spend (a 278% year-over-year increase, with $670,000 concentrated in Q4 2019) [Finding #441] and Deutsche Bank lobbied on anti-money-laundering regulation in 2007 while maintaining more than forty Epstein-linked accounts [Finding #441]. FEC records returned zero contributions for the network's foreign-national associates, including Terje Rød-Larsen, Ehud Barak, and Amir Dossal, consistent with the federal foreign-national prohibition [Finding #477].

sections.title: Cross-Thread Activity and Temporal Concentration
sections.content:
Temporal analysis of investigation findings identifies several windows in which the network's threads — core operational, banking, Apollo and Leon Black finance, Gulf-state contacts, and DOJ-adjacent legal defense — activated in parallel [Finding #3479]. Cross-reference of 73 findings across seven threads indicates 2013 was a peak operational year, with concentrated activity from Alessandro Benedetti (10 findings), Bill Siegel (6), Eduardo Teodorani-Fabbri (6), Ariane de Rothschild (5), Leon Black (4), and IPI (4) [Finding #3479]. In the same year, Paul Weiss drafted a Black service agreement, Dechert handled an IPI fee discrepancy, Deutsche Bank onboarded Epstein in August, and IPI–Nikolic wiring occurred in June [Finding #3479].

Cross-reference of October–December 2016 findings identifies 40 events distributed across five threads, with the Gulf-state thread reaching approximately 30% of activity — the highest ratio in any analyzed period [Finding #3483]. The same period included Kuhn Foundation meetings, an introduction of Jabor Al Thani to the network, Peter Thiel–Churkin–Epstein contacts, Erika Kellerhals's Deutsche Bank KYC review, exchanges with reporter Landon Thomas Jr., and SoftBank-related awareness via Al Thani [Finding #3483]; CBP enhanced screening began on December 1, 2016 [Finding #3483].

Cross-reference of January 26–29, 2019 records identifies 34 findings concentrated in a single week, spanning core operational, Deutsche Bank, and Gulf-state threads [Finding #3481]. In that window Epstein discussed an SDNY RICO investigation with Reid Weingarten, raised Carlos Ghosn and Rajeev Misra with Brad Karp, asked Eduardo Teodorani-Fabbri about Benedetti, and referenced "the SoftBank caper" [Finding #3481]. In June 2020, four findings concerning Attorney General William Barr and four concerning the Edmond de Rothschild Bank appeared in the 30-day window preceding Ghislaine Maxwell's July 2 arrest [Finding #3480], including Barr's June 19 attempt to remove SDNY U.S. Attorney Geoffrey Berman, Berman's refusal, Audrey Strauss's succession, Aaron Zelinsky's June 24 testimony on Stone interference, and a July 1 EdR Bank forfeiture filing [Finding #3480]. Cross-reference of those eight findings indicates the only 2020 period in which the DOJ-adjacent thread and core thread activated simultaneously [Finding #3480].

sections.title: Documented Relationships in the Connection Set
sections.content:
Three connections recorded in the investigation database illustrate how the network linked to media, academia, and intra-network cash movement [Finding #623] [Finding #1535]. According to connection record 1756, New York Times reporter Landon Thomas Jr. emailed Epstein on October 17, 2016 asking whether his story on Abraaj would secure him a meeting, an exchange the investigation logs as a financial-type connection reflecting trade of editorial output for access [Finding #3483].

According to connection record 1776, former Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers wrote a recommendation letter for Nicole Junkermann at Epstein's request in July 2014, which Epstein then forwarded to Lesley Groff — a corporate-type connection reflecting Epstein's intermediary role between academic and financial figures [Finding #441].

According to connection record 1880, an internal funds transfer of $220,000 from Forums LLC to Ghislaine Maxwell's JPMorgan Private Bank checking account in January 2006 is documented in EFTA01524286 [EFTA01524286], situating Forums LLC inside the network's intra-entity payment flow [Finding #623]. These three connections, drawn from a much larger relationship graph, are the subset already encoded in the dossier's connection set [Finding #623] [Finding #1535].

sections.title: Post-Arrest and Post-Mortem State
sections.content:
Comparative 990 review across the network's nonprofit tier indicates that entities under direct Epstein control entered dormancy or sustained decline after the July 2019 arrest and August 2019 death, while entities with independent governance continued to operate [Finding #447]. Gratitude America froze at $8.175 million in assets with zero activity from 2020 onward [Finding #447] [Finding #1535]; the Humpty Dumpty Institute recorded an approximately 80% revenue decline from its $1.8 million peak [Finding #1535]; the Edge Foundation declined from $501,000 to $74,000 in assets [Finding #1535]; and the Dubin Family Foundation wound down from $806,000 to $4,000 [Finding #1535]. By contrast, the Wexner Foundation remained stable at $10–15 million per year, the See Forever Foundation recovered to $4.8 million in assets by 2023, and the Ricardo O'Gorman Garden grew [Finding #447].

Three Epstein-controlled USVI foundations — the J Epstein VI Foundation, Enhanced Education, and the COUQ Foundation — remain absent from federal IRS 990 filings, which leaves their assets, governance, and disbursements outside the federal transparency regime [Finding #447]. Total identifiable nonprofit assets across the network declined by approximately 60% from a 2010–2014 peak of roughly $50–60 million to roughly $16 million by 2022 [Finding #462].
